task: Control Plane Unit 2: release decomposition, canonical release-unit manifests, and batch transplant orchestration.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Projected Release Risk can already identify an invalid pre-code scope, but the Control Plane cannot yet convert that blocked scope into dependency-safe executable release units with canonical manifests and leased batch materialization, so operators must manually split work and can accidentally separate runtime, proof, authority or generated-artifact obligations.
observableOutcomes: A planned scope that violates the unchanged Release Risk Budget is classified before implementation and either decomposed into valid release units or rejected with a fail-closed reason.

Every generated release unit manifest carries transaction identity, target-base lease, ordered file operations, dependency files, authorities, subsystems, required gates and proof, forbidden paths, prerequisites, expected state and reconciliation policy.

Files connected by repository dependency, proof, authority or explicit generated-artifact obligations remain in the same atomic release component whenever separation would make the unit non-functional or non-provable.
Materialization validates the entire manifest before mutation, rejects main drift, rename/delete/read-only violations and stale generated artifacts, and never reports partial application as success.
A successor unit can be reconciled against the newly merged predecessor main state without reusing the predecessor target-base lease.
unresolvedRisks: Atlas relationships can contain broad consumer edges that make a component conservatively larger than a human would choose; Unit 2 must prefer a fail-closed oversized component over silently weakening dependency safety.

Generated artifacts do not all share one regeneration command today, so the manifest contract must support explicit regenerate semantics or a sealed source identity instead of guessing how to recreate them.

Repository materialization is intentionally local Git transaction preparation in this unit; remote merge authority and final production release authority remain outside the materializer and continue to require existing gates.

in: Extend the existing projected Release Risk producer with dependency-aware release decomposition using the existing Atlas semantic/import graph and canonical risk policy.
Produce canonical release-unit manifests containing ordered create/modify/rename/delete operations, dependency/proof/authority obligations and predecessor reconciliation metadata.

Add one repository-level manifest-driven materializer that preflights the whole unit, enforces target-base lease and forbidden/read-only scope, detects already-applied operations and applies the unit as one controlled batch.
Bind decomposition outputs into the existing gate ecosystem and release manifest without creating a parallel truth, risk or quality authority.

Add adversarial regression coverage for the Product Owner scenarios including 30-file split, inseparable dependency scope, cycles, drift, rename/delete, generated artifacts, already-applied changes and proof co-location.
out: Do not change Release Risk Budget thresholds, weights, subsystem limits or high-risk isolation rules.
Do not weaken Completion Truth, Sentinel, Atlas exact-head requirements or any existing blocking guard.
Do not activate parked workforce AAL2 enforcement or edit Auth Core business runtime.
Do not auto-merge release units or grant the materializer production deployment authority.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Release decomposition becomes an execution-routing authority: a false split can create non-functional intermediate main states, detach proof from the capability it proves, or transplant protected authority files. Therefore the strongest practical planning, adversarial and exact-state proof profile is required, while final merge, Release Risk, Completion Truth and production proof remain independently authoritative.

acceptanceCriteria: Projected Release Risk BLOCK produces a deterministic decomposition attempt before implementation rather than only a late error.
Decomposition groups dependency/proof/authority-coupled files into atomic components and never splits a proof file away from the capability files it proves when the Atlas relationship is known.
Every accepted release unit independently satisfies the unchanged canonical Release Risk Budget and names its predecessor and target-base reconciliation rule.
No-safe-decomposition, atomic-component-over-budget and cyclic release-unit dependency states fail closed with machine-readable diagnostics.

Release unit manifests explicitly represent create, modify, rename and delete operations plus required dependencies, authorities, subsystems, gates, evidence, forbidden paths, generated-artifact semantics and expected post-unit state.

Materialization refuses a stale target-base lease, an operation outside manifest scope, forbidden/read-only paths, unresolved rename/delete sources and generated artifacts without regenerate or sealed identity semantics.
Already-applied operations are recognized idempotently, but mixed partial state cannot be reported as a successful fresh application.
Successor-unit reconciliation replaces the predecessor lease with the newly observed main SHA and recomputes applicability rather than copying stale predecessor facts.

Runtime-equivalent Preview anchor discovery scans the complete equivalence segment back to the first runtime-drift boundary instead of truncating at an arbitrary short commit window; a safety-cap overflow fails closed.
invariants: deploy/release-risk-policy.json remains the sole Release Risk threshold and subsystem classification authority.
Atlas remains the repository relationship authority; decomposition consumes its graph and must not maintain a second dependency map.
Guard registry remains the gate identity and producer/consumer authority; release-unit manifests reference its results rather than inventing duplicate gate definitions.
A release unit must be independently buildable or provable with every machine-known required companion file assigned to that unit or an already-merged predecessor.
Target-base SHA is a lease, not documentation: any mismatch with current HEAD blocks materialization.
Rename and delete are first-class operations and preserve source-path identity for reconciliation and proof.
Generated artifacts require either a declared regeneration instruction or sealed source identity; opaque copy semantics are forbidden.
A materializer may touch only paths named by its manifest and may never silently broaden scope.
Final exact-diff Release Risk, exact-head proof, Completion Truth and Lifecycle remain authoritative after decomposition.
A runtime-equivalent READY Preview that is an ancestor of the selected runtime source cannot disappear solely because more quality-only commits were added after it.

failureModes: A 30-file development envelope exceeds the risk budget and a naive chunker separates a runtime file from its required dependency or proof.
A single dependency-connected atomic component contains a high-risk subsystem plus another substantive subsystem and cannot legally fit any release unit.
Two candidate release units depend on each other after grouping, producing a cyclic predecessor graph with no safe first unit.
Main advances after unit one merges but unit two still targets the predecessor base and would overwrite or omit intervening changes.
A rename or delete is flattened into create/modify semantics and leaves the old path or stale consumers behind.
A generated artifact is copied from an obsolete source identity instead of being regenerated or sealed.
The predecessor already applied the same content and the successor materializer duplicates the change instead of treating it as idempotently satisfied.
A protected Auth Core or other read-only authority path enters a generated unit through dependency closure and would be transplanted without explicit authorization.
A fixed commit-count Preview candidate horizon expires after many quality-only commits even though an older READY Preview is still runtime-equivalent and previously proved.
edgeCases: Thirty neutral test/evidence files may travel with substantive components without increasing risk, but must still follow proof co-location requirements.
Several medium-risk subsystems may each be legal alone while their combined score exceeds the budget and therefore require deterministic binning.
A rename whose destination is already identical can be already-applied only if the source path is absent as expected.
A delete already absent at the reconciled target base is idempotently satisfied only when predecessor history or manifest policy permits already-applied recognition.
A successor manifest generated before its predecessor merge must be reconciled and re-leased rather than materialized unchanged.
The valid Preview anchor may be more than forty quality-only commits behind the runtime source while the runtime closure is byte-equivalent.

alternatives.summary: Split blocked development scope into fixed-size groups of files.
alternatives.reason: File counts contain no dependency, authority, proof or risk semantics and can create invalid intermediate states.

alternatives.summary: Keep projected risk as a blocker and require the operator to hand-author every release slice.
alternatives.reason: This repeats machine-known Atlas and gate reasoning downstream, is slow for large scopes and cannot guarantee reproducible manifests.

alternatives.summary: Extend the existing Control Plane chain with Atlas-coupled atomic components, RRB-constrained release units and canonical leased manifests.
alternatives.reason: It preserves existing authorities, moves deterministic split knowledge upstream and enables safe batch execution without a parallel quality system.

specialistReviews.finding: Release decomposition must consume Atlas semantic/import relationships and guard producer-consumer contracts rather than introducing a separate dependency registry.
specialistReviews.resolution: Build atomic components from existing graph edges and canonical proof/authority obligations, with unresolved relationships failing closed.

specialistReviews.finding: Automatic splitting could become a hidden bypass of the Release Risk Budget if a decomposer optimizes toward PASS by altering classification or omitting companion files.
specialistReviews.resolution: Treat deploy/release-risk-policy.json as immutable input; evaluate every atomic component and resulting unit through the existing evaluateReleaseRiskFiles semantics and reject any component that cannot legally fit.

specialistReviews.finding: Recent Control Plane failures came from downstream recomputation, stale identity and classifier self-narrowing; decomposition can repeat those failure classes if manifests recalculate upstream facts independently.
specialistReviews.resolution: Persist upstream Atlas/risk/gate provenance into release manifests and require successor reconciliation against fresh main rather than copying stale calculated state.

specialistReviews.finding: Twenty or thirty per-file API operations are operationally fragile and can leave ambiguous partial state after interruption.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use one manifest-driven repository batch materializer with whole-unit preflight, leased base identity and explicit idempotency status before any mutation.

challenge.scenario: A planned envelope contains 30 files across multiple legal medium/low subsystems.
challenge.finding: Fixed-size chunks can exceed RRB or sever dependency/proof companions despite equal file counts.
challenge.resolution: Create atomic dependency groups first, then deterministically pack those groups under unchanged RRB constraints.

challenge.scenario: One high-risk subsystem is planned together with another substantive subsystem.
challenge.finding: The current policy requires high-risk isolation, so preserving the original scope in one release is invalid.
challenge.resolution: Place the high-risk atomic component in an isolated unit and move unrelated components to successor units; fail if a required companion creates an inseparable cross-subsystem component.

challenge.scenario: Several medium-risk subsystems collectively exceed maxPoints while every subsystem is individually legal.
challenge.finding: Subsystem-count-only decomposition can still produce a score violation.
challenge.resolution: Evaluate candidate unit risk after every atomic-component placement and start a new unit when the next component would block.

challenge.scenario: Two files are coupled by Atlas imports and the consumer is required for the planned capability.
challenge.finding: Separating them can leave an intermediate main state that compiles but does not implement or prove the intended behavior.
challenge.resolution: Union dependency/proof-required files into one atomic component before risk packing.

challenge.scenario: Release-unit prerequisites form A -> B -> A after grouping.
challenge.finding: No unit has a valid predecessor-free execution order and arbitrary ordering would hide a cycle.
challenge.resolution: Topologically validate the unit graph and return FAIL_CLOSED with a cycle diagnostic.

challenge.scenario: Unit one merges and main changes before unit two materialization.
challenge.finding: The old unit-two lease no longer proves the target repository state.
challenge.resolution: Require successor reconciliation to the observed new main SHA and block unchanged stale manifests.

challenge.scenario: The manifest contains rename and delete operations plus already-applied content from a predecessor.
challenge.finding: Flattening operations loses source identity while blindly replaying duplicates can corrupt history or fail unnecessarily.
challenge.resolution: Model operation types explicitly and classify each as pending or already-applied during whole-manifest preflight.

challenge.scenario: Dependency closure pulls an Auth Core/read-only authority file into a proposed unit or leaves a proof file in another unit.
challenge.finding: Automatic closure can accidentally grant write scope to protected authority or make a unit unverifiable.
challenge.resolution: Protected paths remain forbidden even when referenced; proof/required companion edges co-locate writable files, while protected dependencies must already exist in the target base or decomposition fails.

challenge.scenario: A generated artifact is present but its source identity is stale or no regeneration instruction is known.
challenge.finding: Copying it would create a structurally valid but semantically stale unit.
challenge.resolution: Require regenerate semantics or an explicit sealed source hash/source commit and fail closed otherwise.

challenge.scenario: No partition of the atomic components can satisfy the unchanged Release Risk Budget.
challenge.finding: Forcing any split would create a knowingly invalid release topology.
challenge.resolution: Return NO_SAFE_DECOMPOSITION and keep execution unauthorized for that scope rather than weakening a gate.

challenge.scenario: The current runtime source has no Preview because quality-only commits are intentionally Vercel-cancelled, while a previously successful runtime-equivalent Preview is fifty-seven commits behind it.
challenge.finding: A fixed forty-commit candidate horizon falsely reports TEMPLATE_LIVE_RUNTIME_PREVIEW_ANCHOR_MISSING even though ancestry and zero runtime drift prove a safe Preview exists.
challenge.resolution: Walk the runtime-equivalent ancestry until the first runtime-drift boundary, retain all equivalent candidate SHAs within a high safety cap, and fail closed if the semantic boundary cannot be reached before that cap.

proofPlan: Require Plan Before Code PASS on the plan-only head before the first implementation edit and preserve the exact main base lease.
Add adversarial unit tests covering 30-file decomposition, high-risk isolation, medium-score overflow, inseparable dependencies and no-safe-decomposition failure.
Prove cyclic release-unit prerequisites fail closed and deterministic legal units receive a stable predecessor order.
Prove rename, delete, generated artifact and already-applied operations retain explicit first-class manifest semantics.
Prove target-base drift blocks materialization before any worktree mutation and a successor reconcile operation replaces the stale lease.
Prove forbidden/read-only Auth Core paths cannot be materialized even when they appear through dependency closure.
Prove proof files and machine-required companion files remain co-located with the capability unit or are satisfied by an already-merged predecessor.
Require Edit-Time Guard, Incremental Replay and final Release Risk PASS without any policy threshold or classifier weakening.
Run full Quality Tests, TypeScript and Production Build on the exact implementation head.
Require exact-head Completion Truth VERIFIED, Lifecycle Closure PASS and Template Factory external proof when canonical guard applicability requires it.

Prove Preview-anchor discovery includes a runtime-equivalent candidate beyond forty metadata-only commits, stops at the first runtime-drift boundary, and fails closed on ancestry-scan overflow rather than silently truncating.

requirements.requirement: An over-budget planned scope is decomposed before implementation into dependency-safe release units or fails closed when no legal decomposition exists.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Decomposition must not weaken or bypass the canonical Release Risk Budget.

requirements.requirement: Every release unit receives a canonical manifest with leased base identity, explicit file operations, dependencies, authority, gate, proof, forbidden-path and reconciliation semantics.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The release unit manifest may not become a second manually maintained dependency or gate authority.

requirements.requirement: Manifest-driven batch materialization validates the whole unit and target-base lease before mutation, supports create/modify/rename/delete and never reports partial application as success.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Stale lease, protected scope or partial mutation must never be accepted as a successful unit materialization.

requirements.requirement: A successor release unit reconciles against the newly merged predecessor main state and cannot reuse a stale target-base lease or stale machine-derived obligations.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A successor unit may not materialize from the predecessor's obsolete base identity.

notes: Unit 2 scope was reconciled after exact-head Template Factory proof exposed a fixed-horizon Preview-anchor false negative. Proof-engine changes remain forbidden until this expanded plan passes Plan Before Code.
